name: Vidyānanda
dates_notes: Conventionally assigned to the late eighth or early ninth century from his place after Akalaṅka and before later Digambara authors; the precise span is uncertain.
core_thesis: Vidyānanda extends mature Digambara dialectics through detailed commentaries on Samantabhadra and Akalaṅka. His work develops the Jaina defense of multi-aspectual reality, conditional predication, and the authority of the omniscient Jina in sustained engagement with Buddhist and Brahmanical philosophical positions.

engaged_works.title: Ashtasahasri
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Vidyānanda's large commentary on Akalaṅka's *Aṣṭaśatī*, itself a commentary on Samantabhadra's *Āpta-Mīmāṃsā*. The nested commentarial relation should not be reversed.
engaged_works.summary: A major Digambara commentary that develops Akalaṅka's reading of Samantabhadra's *Āpta-Mīmāṃsā*, including its defense of the Jina as a trustworthy source and its critique of one-sided philosophical claims.

engaged_works.title: Tattvartha-Sloka-Varttika
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Vidyānanda's extended engagement with the *Tattvārthasūtra* and Akalaṅka's commentary.
engaged_works.summary: An extensive scholastic treatment of the *Tattvārthasūtra* in dialogue with the Digambara commentary tradition. It is a principal source for mature Jaina epistemology and dialectics.
